reason: E2 confirms Cr-V precipitate formation in the baseline alloy at 8 dpa, but the cited evidence does not mention Hf, sluggish diffusion, or any mechanism by which Hf suppresses precipitation; the claim that Hf suppresses precipitates relies on a different alloy (W29Ta42Cr5V16Hf8) not cited here, and no evidence supports the lattice-strain/sluggish-diffusion mechanism or retained manufacturability.
premises: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops Cr-V-rich precipitates under irradiation near 8 dpa
Hf addition to a similar W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy suppressed dislocation loops and precipitates at 10 dpa
Hf can induce lattice strain and sluggish diffusion in refractory HEAs
Partial replacement of Cr by Hf retains bulk manufacturability
Suppressing Cr-V clustering will maintain low hardening and radiation resistance
